Summarise a trace

Source: R/core-ledger-core.R
hr_trace_summary.Rd

Summarise a trace

Usage

hr_trace_summary(trace)

Arguments

trace

A gr_trace.

Value

A one-row data frame: run_id, calls, cached, steps, tokens_in, tokens_out, errors, elapsed_s, embed_calls, embed_tokens, tokens_reasoning, tokens_cached_in, usage_estimated, request_s, local_s, overhead_s, request_share, local_share, overhead_share.

calls counts every request, including the embed_calls of them made to an embeddings endpoint. tokens_in and tokens_out are the size of the model calls' prompts and replies; the text sent to be embedded is counted in embed_tokens instead, because an embedding model is priced at a small fraction of a chat model's rate. There is no cost column: hr_trace_cost() prices every request at its own model, embeddings included, and is what the run cost. Combining tokens_in/tokens_out with hr_estimate_cost() estimates the model calls alone at one model's prices.

cached is how many of those calls were answered from an hr_cache() or a hr_replay_client(). Their tokens are still counted in tokens_in and tokens_out, because that is how large the prompts and replies were; they were simply not paid for again. A run with cached == calls cost nothing, so feeding its token counts to hr_estimate_cost() gives you what the run would have cost, not what it did.

errors counts every failed request, including any the run recovered from (see errors in hr_trace()).

tokens_reasoning and tokens_cached_in are the reasoning tokens and cached input tokens the provider reported for the model calls, 0 where it reported none. They are parts of tokens_out and tokens_in, not additions to them. usage_estimated is the share of requests whose token counts were estimated locally because the provider reported none (see tokens under "Steps" in hr_trace()), from 0 to 1, or NA when no request says. The share of input tokens the provider served from its cache is tokens_cached_in / tokens_in; the trace's print shows it when it is above 0.

elapsed_s is the time from the run's start (trace$started) to the end of its last step: a request's ended_utc, or the at time of a local step. at is local time with no offset, so it is placed using the offset the trace's requests show (their at beside their ended_utc), or the utc_offset the trace recorded when it holds no request. It is read from the steps, so a summary taken an hour after the run, or of a trace saved with saveRDS() and read back in another time zone, gives the same figure. A trace with local steps, no request and no utc_offset (one made by harnessr 0.7.0) cannot place them: its elapsed_s is then request_s + local_s. A trace with no steps gives 0.

The last six columns split that time. request_s is the seconds the requests took (model calls and embeddings requests, retries included), local_s the seconds local steps recorded (a command step from hr_step_command() records its run time; segmentation, truncation and other local steps record none, so their time falls into the overhead), and overhead_s the rest of elapsed_s. Requests sent in parallel overlap, so request_s can pass elapsed_s, and overhead_s is then 0. The three shares are each part over the three together, so they add to 1, or NA when no time was measured.

See also

hr_trace(), as_json(), hr_trace_cost(), hr_estimate_cost(), hr_cache()

Examples

cl <- hr_mock_client(function(m, p) "45.2 million dollars")
ans <- answer_document(gr_example(), "What was revenue?", "thorough", client = cl)
#> Using cached ingestion for this document + settings.
#> Segmenting with 'paragraph' (cap 1200 tokens, overlap 120).
#> Reading with 'map_reduce' (all|N+logN|tree) over 1 chunk(s).
hr_trace_summary(ans$trace)
#>                          run_id calls cached steps tokens_in tokens_out errors
#> 1 run_20261127060256.939_9b6999     1      0     4       607         10      0
#>   elapsed_s embed_calls embed_tokens tokens_reasoning tokens_cached_in
#> 1      0.03           0            0                0                0
#>   usage_estimated request_s local_s overhead_s request_share local_share
#> 1               1         0       0       0.03        0.0344           0
#>   overhead_share
#> 1         0.9656

# What the run cost, each request priced at its own model (nothing, for a
# mock), and what its model calls would cost at another model's prices.
# harnessr ships no prices, so set that model's first. The figures are
# illustrative: use your provider's current prices.
hr_trace_cost(ans$trace)
#>        model calls paid_calls paid_in paid_out usd paid_reasoning
#> 1 mock-model     1          1     607       10   0              0
#>   paid_cached_in priced   as_of certain
#> 1              0   TRUE 2026-11    TRUE
hr_register_model("gpt-4o", input_usd = 2.50, output_usd = 10)
hr_estimate_cost("gpt-4o", ans$trace$tokens_in, ans$trace$tokens_out)
#> [1] 0.0016175
